```markdown
---
name: generating-release-notes
description: Invoke when the user asks for release notes, a changelog, or "what changed since the last release". Collect commits since the latest git tag, group by conventional-commit type, and write RELEASE_NOTES.md at the repo root using the section order and entry format in this skill.
---

# Generating Release Notes

## Procedure

1. Find the last release tag:
   ```bash
   git describe --tags --abbrev=0
   ```
   If no tag exists, ask the user for the starting ref. Do not silently use the full history.
2. Collect commits in range:
   ```bash
   git log <tag>..HEAD --oneline
   ```
   Also check commit bodies (`git log <tag>..HEAD --format='%s%n%b'`) for a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. Treat those commits as breaking.
3. Group commits by conventional-commit type using the mapping below. Each group becomes a section.
4. Write `RELEASE_NOTES.md` at the repo root.

## Commit Type Mapping

| Type | Section |
|------|---------|
| any type with `!` (e.g. `feat!`) | Breaking Changes |
| `security` scope on any type (e.g. `fix(security)`) | Security |
| `feat` | Features |
| `perf` | Performance |
| `fix` | Bug Fixes |
| `revert` | Reverts. Also remove the reverted entry if it is in the same release |
| `refactor` | Omit unless user-facing |
| `docs`, `chore`, `ci`, `build` | Omit |

## Output Rules

- Section order: Breaking Changes, Security, Features, Performance, Bug Fixes, Reverts.
- Omit empty sections.
- One line per entry, imperative mood, no trailing period.
- Every entry links its PR number as `[#123]`. If a commit has no PR number, list it without the link and tell the user which entries are missing one.
```

**What I left out, and why.** All of your operational work is in the file above: the procedure, every row of the type mapping, every precedence rule, and every output rule. Three parts of the documentation are not in it:

- **Background.** It defines release notes, semver, and git tags. Claude already knows these.
- **History.** The Confluence → shell script → Priya's rewrite → March retirement story doesn't change what Claude does.
- **The closing endorsement.** It isn't an instruction Claude can act on.

The SKILL.md body loads into context every time the skill activates. Content Claude can't act on costs tokens on every run and dilutes the instructions that matter, so including it would make the skill worse, not more complete. The history is still worth keeping. A better home for it is your team wiki or the PR that introduces this skill, where people will actually read it.

**Small additions I made**, so you can review them:
- A no-tag fallback: ask the user for a starting ref. Otherwise `git describe` fails on repos with no tags.
- A `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer check. `--oneline` hides commit bodies, and conventional commits allows marking breaking changes in the footer instead of with `!`.
- A missing-PR-number rule. Your docs require `[#123]` on every entry but don't say what to do when a commit has none.
